## Summary

**The gap P17-FLIP-01 recorded is closed for real.** P21.9 delivered the P17
*pathway* connectors and honestly left `SIG-INGEST-049*` PARTIAL — municipal
surveillance-ordinance (CCOPS) disclosures are a different source class, not the
pathways ingestion. This ticket lands that class:

- **`government_mandated_disclosure` is its own source class** (SIG-INGEST-049):
  `licence: public record`, `format: pdf`, `extraction: document_pipeline` —
  distinct from `civil_society_dataset` and `vendor_portal`. A new
  `SourceKind.GOVERNMENT_MANDATED_DISCLOSURE` enum member is carried by the
  class-level `ccops_ordinance_disclosures` row plus the three paying sources
  (`ccops_seattle`, `ccops_nyc_post`, `ccops_sf`); the class posture is also
  registered as data in the connector vocab.
- **Depth, not breadth, honestly** (SIG-INGEST-049a): the scope row is data a
  test pins — ~26 jurisdictions ≈ 5% of the US population / ~0.14% of US
  law-enforcement agencies, ZERO machine-readable outputs, the canonical
  national list a JPEG on the ACLU page, `registry_row_cap: 26`. Its highest
  use is calibration, not coverage (SIG-INGEST-049d).
- **One connector, three paying source adapters** (SIG-INGEST-049c, the
  ADR-071 precedent): `field_questionnaire` (Seattle SMC 14.18 — the fixed
  ~50-field SIR), `policy_clauses` (NYC POST Act — the layer-3 `pdf_text`
  clause locator), `inventory_table` (SF Chapter 19B biannual citywide
  inventory + compliance metric).
- **Per-agency AGGREGATE rows only** (Part VIII): every claim is keyed
  `ccops:<jurisdiction>:<agency>` and must carry `agency` + `reporting_period`
  + `technology` (ordinance claims exempt) — `assert_aggregate_row` refuses
  missing fields, forbidden person-level columns (plate / person / per-search /
  officer / device-serial), forbidden tokens, and person-naming predicates
  outright. A schema gate, not a policy note.
- **`procured ≠ deployed`, two mechanical layers** (RISK-P21-16 applied to the
  class): the use predicates (`in_use`, `usage_count`, `complaint_count`,
  `deployment_location`, `effectiveness_claim`) ride only on `disclosure_use`
  claims; and `disclosure_use`/`compliance_finding` claims require a document
  that *itself reports actual use* — a `deployment_report` genre, or a mandated
  disclosure carrying `reports_actual_use` (SF's inventory, whose own rows mark
  technologies "in use without an approved policy") — **never** a
  `procurement_record` or `vendor_disclosure` genre however labelled. The genre
  is re-derived from the document text, never trusted from a fixture label.
  Within a use-reporting disclosure the distinction stays row-level: an
  `approved` / `seeking_procurement_or_pilot` status yields an
  `inventory_entry` claim and nothing more.
- **Mandated ≠ populated is recorded** (F3.20): `answered` /
  `present_but_empty` / `absent` — Seattle's blank Fiscal 1.1/1.2 cost tables
  land as `disclosure_field_state` claims, never fabricated values.
- **The non-compliance finding is first-class** (SIG-INGEST-049e): SF's
  `compliance_finding` claims carry `in_use_without_policy_count=37`,
  `policy_compliance_share=0.66`, and the verbatim "26% in use without an
  approved policy" finding — a claim class available nowhere else.
- **049f / 050 land honestly**: the committed seed asset
  `data/state_alpr_statute_seed.toml` (NCSL — 16 states / 17 table rows / 21
  enactments, `as_of: 2022-02-03`, `frozen`, `never_a_feed`) and the
  future-due `future_statutory_disclosure_2027` row (commencement date
  2027-04-01) are pinned by tests.

## The connector-class design (ADR-080)

`connectors.government_mandated_disclosure` — a single registered connector
(`@register`) whose `extract` dispatches on the document `kind` to per-source
extractors. All claims route through `disclosure_claim`, which runs **all three
guards** (predicate allowlist → genre/use gate → aggregate schema) so no
extractor can bypass them; `normalize` sweeps the emitted set again and stamps
the vocab version; `load` adds `claim_id`/`sys_period` (the two
non-deterministic columns, excluded from the replay fingerprint).

## Aggregate-row schema

| field | rule |
|---|---|
| `subject_id` | `ccops:<jurisdiction>:<agency>` (ordinance: `ccops:<jurisdiction>`) |
| `agency`, `reporting_period` | required on every claim |
| `technology` | required on every non-`ordinance` claim |
| `aggregate_level` | stamped `agency_technology_period` |
| forbidden columns | plate / person / per-search / per-incident / officer / device-serial / … → `NonAggregateRow` |
| forbidden tokens / person-naming | → `PartVIIIViolation` / `PersonNamingRefused` |

## `procured ≠ deployed` enforcement

| edge | rule | test |
|---|---|---|
| predicate level | use predicates only on `disclosure_use` | `test_deployment_predicate_on_a_non_use_claim_is_refused` |
| document level | use/compliance needs deployment genre OR `reports_actual_use` | `test_use_claim_from_a_non_use_disclosure_is_refused` / `…_is_admitted` ×2 |
| never-use genres | procurement/vendor can never report use, flag or no flag | `test_procurement_genre_never_reports_use_however_labelled` |
| row level | only `in_use_statuses` yield `in_use` | `test_sf_inventory_emits_use_only_for_in_use_statuses` (5 rows, none for approved/seeking) |
| commitment docs | SIR / POST IUP emit zero use claims | `test_no_use_claim_from_a_commitment_or_policy_document` |
| mislabels | declared genre ≠ derived → rejected | `test_mislabelled_genre_is_rejected_genre_is_re_derived` |
